sections.title: The letters oi
paragraphs: The letters oi usually make one diphthong. A diphthong is two vowel sounds in one syllable. You hear this sound in the word (oil) /ɔɪl/. Oil is a thick liquid used for fuel or cooking. These two letters make two different sounds in English words.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: Start with your lips open and round. Pull your tongue back and down in your mouth. Then glide your tongue up and forward. Your lips unround and spread wide into a smile. Touch your throat to feel your voice shake. For the other sound, round your lips tightly. Open quickly to a wide open vowel with your tongue low.

sections.title: Spelling patterns
paragraphs: In most English words, these letters make the main gliding vowel sound. You see this sound in words like (coin) /kɔɪn/. In words taken from French, these letters make a different sound. You can hear this French sound in the word (memoir) /mɛm.wɑː/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not turn the letters oi into two separate beats. Glide smoothly from the first vowel to the second vowel in one syllable. Do not drop the second part of the sound. Remember to keep the French sound in borrowed words like (memoir) /mɛm.wɑː/ instead of the common diphthong.
